assessment.nobel_worthiness: First-principles molecular dynamics put electronic structure and atomic motion on one footing, opening ab initio simulation of liquids, interfaces, reactions and condensed matter. Originality is unmistakable and the method underlies decades of quantitative theory-experiment comparison, which is the standard I apply to theory.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 Car-Parrinello paper is a clean two-person credit; the supplied names support a prize without the three-person squeeze.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use, countless independent implementations and validations; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Chemistry-versus-physics framing of the prize and possible competition with other methods-development candidates.
Parrinello also appears under other candidates, so a combined theory prize would need careful allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation of proteins by PROTACs and molecular glues is a genuinely new pharmacological modality with real clinical consequences, a game-changer in the sense I look for. It is chemistry-driven and conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) made the founding PROTAC concept; Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands made it a practical chemical tool. Handa and Ito's cereblon-thalidomide work is an alternative molecular-glue contribution, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials, but approvals are not yet established, so the clinical payoff is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the molecular-glue (cereblon) discoveries need separate recognition.
Absence of approved PROTAC drugs at this point; I cannot verify current clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single nucleotides without double-strand breaks, a chemically conceived solution that is already used in the clinic and across research. It is a clear game-changer for genome engineering.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the unambiguous leader; Komor and Gaudelli made the cytosine and adenine base editors as the lead trainees, which fits a three-person configuration. Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID is a parallel but less central contribution.
assessment.maturity: Rapid independent adoption and first human trials give strong confirmation, though long-term clinical safety data are still limited.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prime-editing candidate and with the earlier CRISPR prize.
Credit for Target-AID versus the Liu-lab editors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum accuracy at classical cost, transforming what can be simulated in materials and chemistry. This extends my own field and I judge it as game-changing, provided the quantitative links to experiment hold.
assessment.attribution: Behler (neural-network potentials, with Parrinello) and Csányi with Bartók (Gaussian approximation potentials) are the original architectures; Parrinello, Weinan E and von Lilienfeld are also strong claimants, so some real contributors would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Adoption is wide and rapid but the field is still evolving, and generalisation and transferability are not fully settled; arguably early.
uncertainties: Transferability and reliability beyond training domains.
Hard to select three from a crowded and fast-moving field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached high efficiency in a decade, a rare materials discovery with strong practical consequences and rich solid-state chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park the solid-state 2012 device and Snaith the thin-film breakthrough; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have strong claims too, making a three-person split contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are replicated widely, but long-term stability and commercial deployment remain unresolved, so timing may be premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase explain biological nitrogen fixation and its unusual FeMo-cofactor, a central problem in enzymology and bioinorganic chemistry, directly relevant to how enzymes catalyse hard reactions.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work, Einsle revealed the central carbide, and Ribbe and Seefeldt contributed assembly and mechanism; Dean's earlier genetics complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding details remain actively debated.
uncertainties: Credit among Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe and Einsle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reshaped how cellular chemistry is organised and has clear impact across biology; the physical-chemistry framing is novel and influential.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the 2009 P-granule discovery; Rosen's multivalent phase-separation work gave a quantitative basis, and Pappu and Mittag are also claimants.
assessment.maturity: The paradigm is widely adopted but still debated in terms of physiological relevance and quantitative mechanisms.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance of phase separation.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology for the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Covalent targeting of mutant KRAS with a cysteine-directed small molecule opened a target long considered undruggable and has produced approved drugs, a clear consequence from a simple chemical idea.
assessment.attribution: Shokat is the decisive originator for both the KRAS G12C inhibitors and the chemical genetics of kinases; a single laureate is supportable, and a second person would be difficult to justify from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical approvals of KRAS G12C inhibitors confirm the concept; the broader limitations of resistance remain under study.
uncertainties: Industry contributions to drug development beyond the academic discovery.
A single-laureate prize may leave the committee wanting a combined configuration.
